title: Approval policy contract with an unconditional human-authority gate
description:
Objective: give moe-next a durable, typed representation of WHEN a submitted plan may proceed without a human, and make certain work incapable of proceeding without one regardless of that setting.

RAISED BY: governor-18a42000 audit, 2026-08-15, at the human's direction, after a live incident on the orchestrating board. Measured on current bytes before filing. (This task replaces task-2212cfd25bbe4cd3a32770987a2b834d, which I deleted for carrying 8 DoD items against the 3-7 target; content is unchanged apart from folding the cross-cutting quality items together.)

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS — do not rebuild it:
- `approvePlan` at packages/core/src/planning/planning-run-submission.ts:172, dispatched as the `plan.approve` command at packages/core/src/planning/planning-run-reducer.ts:174. The approval COMMAND and its reducer arm are landed.
- apps/control-room/src/approvals/approval-gating.ts carries an approval refusal-reason channel, explicitly marked PROVISIONAL pending the daemon's stable reason registry (spec section 13-D2).
- Roughly 70 non-test files reference approval in some form.

WHAT IS ABSENT — measured, each zero non-test hits repo-wide: `approvalMode`, `approvalPolicy`, `ApprovalPolicy`, `requiresApproval`, `autoApprove`, `auto_approve`. A positive control on the identical query shape (`createStoreDependencies`, 3 files) confirms the greps are well scoped and these zeros are real absences rather than a mis-typed path.

THE GAP, stated exactly: moe-next can EXECUTE an approval but cannot EXPRESS AN APPROVAL POLICY. No typed value anywhere answers "may this plan proceed without a human, and under what conditions". Approval is therefore implicit and unrecorded — a property of whoever happens to call plan.approve, not a decision the system holds and can be audited against.

THE INCIDENT THAT MOTIVATES IT, so the shape is grounded rather than abstract. On the orchestrating board on 2026-08-15, every BLOCKED task was promoted to PLANNING inside a two-minute window, clearing each task's recorded blockedReason. Two were release-cutover tasks whose own descriptions name an explicit human authority gate as a hard dependency: a GA activation record requiring GO_ACTIVATE, and a legacy quiesce drill requiring GO_QUIESCE. Neither GO had ever been issued — verified by scanning every message channel. Both became claimable, and that board runs auto-approval on a 2s delay, so no human would have seen a plan before a worker began executing it.

The lesson is NOT "add a global mode". A single project-wide switch would not have prevented this: fast delegation was the correct setting for most of that board, and flipping everything to manual review to protect two tasks is the wrong trade. What was needed is a gate that binds to the WORK, survives a bulk status change that clears other fields, and cannot be satisfied by any agent.

SCOPE — a pure typed contract in @moe/core plus its reducer integration. NOT IN SCOPE: control-room UI, daemon wiring or transport, the external orchestrator's settings file, migrating existing approval call sites, or the provisional reason channel in approval-gating.ts. Those are follow-on consumer tasks; name them rather than building them.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: A closed, frozen ApprovalPolicy vocabulary is published from the @moe/core root, expressing at minimum proceed-without-human (its delay an explicit typed value, never an implicit default) and require-human. The set is exhaustive by construction: adding a member is a compile error at every exhaustive switch over it.

A per-unit-of-work HUMAN AUTHORITY GATE is representable independently of the policy, and when present it refuses regardless of policy - no ApprovalPolicy value or combination can approve gated work. A test enumerates EVERY policy member against a gated unit and asserts refusal for each, pinning a nonzero exact cardinality equal to the vocabulary size so a shrunk enum cannot silently reduce coverage.

Satisfying the gate requires a named human principal and is recorded durably with that principal and the moment it was given. A missing, empty, or non-human principal is refused with an exact stable reason code AND its refusing layer, asserted literally rather than by matching an Error message; where two layers can refuse the same input, the test asserts which one answered.

The landed approvePlan (planning-run-submission.ts:172) and its plan.approve reducer arm (planning-run-reducer.ts:174) keep their current behaviour for ungated work, with their existing tests green and unmodified - the policy composes with them rather than replacing them.

Mutation drills prove the guards are attached to production: removing the human-authority check turns a NAMED test red on the refusal assertion, and independently weakening the principal requirement turns a NAMED test red. Each drill is restored byte-exact and verified by hash.

Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm typecheck exits 0 with each leg's exit code read separately, and the consuming task ids are recorded per Clause 1 - this lands a pure contract and does not itself compose a consumer edge.
taskRails: The human authority gate is the point of this task. It must be UNCONDITIONAL: no policy value, configuration, or agent action may satisfy it. If your design lets any ApprovalPolicy member approve gated work, the design is wrong.

Do not add a project-wide mode as the primary mechanism. A blanket switch is what failed in the motivating incident. The gate binds to the unit of work and must survive a bulk status change that clears other fields.
Assert the reason code, not the outcome: every refusal test pins the exact stable code and the refusing layer. A test asserting only that approval did not happen is one added layer away from vacuous.

A closed vocabulary must be exhaustive by construction, and any sweep over it must assert a nonzero exact cardinality equal to the vocabulary size - a sweep that silently generates zero cases passes while testing nothing.

This is a pure @moe/core contract. Do not wire the daemon, the control room, or the external orchestrator's settings; name the consumer tasks instead. Keep each production source under 250 physical lines and split before 400.

Re-measure the absent symbols before planning. approvalMode, approvalPolicy, ApprovalPolicy, requiresApproval and autoApprove all measured zero non-test hits today, but the tree moves and a duplicate would collide with its owner in this shared worktree.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD — WRITE THE TESTS FIRST. Create `packages/core/src/planning/approval-policy.test.ts`.

VOCABULARY (DoD 1): assert the member NAMES literally and derive only the COUNT from the imported frozen array. An expectation derived from the array under test compares it with itself and survives a rename or a deletion. Assert the array is frozen.

THE UNCONDITIONAL GATE (DoD 2) — the central test. Sweep EVERY policy member against a gated unit of work and assert refusal for each. Pin the generated case count EQUAL to the vocabulary size, derived from the imported array, so a shrunk enum cannot silently reduce coverage. This is the test that proves the gate is not satisfiable by configuration.

CRITICAL: THE GATED CASES MUST OTHERWISE BE VALID APPROVALS — correct witness, matching sealed hashes — so that the ONLY thing that can refuse them is the new gate. A malformed witness would be refused by the existing `illegal` guard, and the test would pass while proving nothing about the gate. Assert WHICH LAYER answered, not merely that approval did not happen.

SATISFACTION (DoD 3): a named human principal satisfies the gate and the satisfaction is recorded durably with that principal and the moment it was given. Missing, empty, and non-human principals are each refused with the EXACT stable code AND its layer, asserted literally — never by matching an Error message.

DELAY IS EXPLICIT (DoD 1): assert a proceed-without-human policy cannot be constructed without stating its delay.

These fail until steps 3-4 land.

implementationPlan.description:
THE POLICY VOCABULARY AND THE GATE (DoD 1, 2, 3). Create `packages/core/src/planning/approval-policy.ts`.

TWO MECHANISMS, BOTH REQUIRED:
- A FROZEN ARRAY of the policy members, for the runtime sweep DoD 2 needs — a test cannot iterate a type.
- A DISCRIMINATED UNION derived from it (`(typeof APPROVAL_POLICIES)[number]` or a tagged union), plus an `assertNever` helper used in EVERY switch over it. Without the `never` assignment TypeScript does not error when a member is added, so the array alone does not deliver DoD 1's "compile error at every exhaustive switch".
Members: at minimum proceed-without-human — with its delay a REQUIRED typed field, never an implicit default, since an unstated auto-approval delay is the incident's actual mechanism — and require-human.

THE HUMAN AUTHORITY GATE IS SEPARATE FROM THE POLICY AND CONSULTED FIRST. It is a per-unit-of-work value, not a policy member and not comparable to one. The decision function checks the gate BEFORE it looks at the policy and short-circuits: no policy value, combination, or agent action can approve gated work (task rail 1). If your design permits any policy member to approve gated work, the design is wrong.

BIND IT TO THE WORK, NOT TO A STATUS, and say so in the module comment. In the motivating incident a bulk status change cleared every task's recorded blockedReason; a gate modelled as another lifecycle field would have been cleared the same way. The next reader will be tempted to model it as a status — the comment is what stops them.

Satisfying the gate REQUIRES a named human principal and produces a durable record carrying that principal and the moment. Refusals carry a stable code from a closed frozen vocabulary AND name their layer.

Add the `.js` bridge. Keep under 250 lines; if it overruns, split the gate into `approval-authority.ts` with its own bridge rather than trimming behaviour.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. 41 tests passed (2 files), VITEST_EXIT=0. CORE_TYPECHECK_EXIT=0.
planning-source-size.test.ts 9 passed — all four new planning files under the 250 ceiling:
approval-authority.ts 167, approval-policy.ts 129, approval-policy.test.ts 171,
approval-authority.test.ts 175. Both .js bridges written (`export * from "./<module>.ts";`).

TWO MECHANISMS, BOTH LANDED, AND COUPLED SO THEY CANNOT DRIFT:
- APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS — Object.freeze(["PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN","REQUIRE_HUMAN"] as const).
  The runtime array DoD 2's sweep iterates.
- ApprovalPolicy — a discriminated union DERIVED from that array via a mapped type over a
  per-member payload interface:
    { [Kind in ApprovalPolicyKind]: { readonly kind: Kind } & ApprovalPolicyPayloads[Kind] }
      [ApprovalPolicyKind]
  A member added to the ARRAY with no payload entry cannot be indexed -> compile error. A member
  added to the UNION without an arm in decidePolicy -> compile error at assertNever. Both
  directions are tsc errors, which is what step 5's D1 drill will confirm.
- delayMs is a REQUIRED field on the PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN arm, so no auto-approval delay can
  default implicitly. The @ts-expect-error test is live: typecheck exit 0 proves the directive is
  consumed, i.e. `{ kind: "PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN" }` really is a type error today.

assertNever RETURNS a refusal rather than throwing. It still produces the `never` compile error
DoD 1 needs, but this contract fails closed and a crash is not a refusal.

THE GATE IS NOT A POLICY MEMBER AND IS CONSULTED FIRST. decideApprovalAuthority reads
request.gate before it ever looks at request.policy and short-circuits: an unsatisfied gate
returns the gate-layer refusal for every policy member; a satisfied gate proceeds with
delayMs 0 carrying the grant. REQUIRE_HUMAN is documented in-module as a policy DEFAULT for
UNGATED work that cannot stand in for the gate.

BOUND TO THE WORK, NOT A STATUS — stated at the top of approval-authority.ts with the incident
that motivates it, because the next reader will otherwise model it as a lifecycle field.
Enforced, not just documented: the grant re-states gateId + workRef and checkHumanAuthority
re-derives the verdict on EVERY read, so a real human grant cannot be carried onto other work
(APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_BINDING_MISMATCH) and an agent that writes the record directly gains
nothing — it cannot name itself HUMAN.

Refusal order is identical in grantHumanAuthority and checkHumanAuthority (principal, then
moment, then binding), so both entry points answer an identical defect with an identical code.

One closed frozen code vocabulary (8) + layer vocabulary (2) covering both layers: a consumer
receives one refusal and needs one registry; `layer` says which answered.

DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN, and why: the plan named ONE production module. Step 1 found
planning-source-size.test.ts caps every .ts in planning/ at 250 lines INCLUDING tests, so I took
the split step 3 pre-authorised ("split the gate into approval-authority.ts with its own bridge
rather than trimming behaviour") and applied it to the tests as well. No behaviour trimmed.

implementationPlan.description:
MUTATION DRILLS (DoD 5). Capture `sha256sum` of each target BEFORE mutating; restore by Edit and verify by `sha256sum` against the captured hash. Never `git checkout` — it reverts to HEAD and destroys this task's untracked new files, and `git diff` is blind to them so an empty diff proves nothing.

D1 — EXHAUSTIVENESS IS A COMPILE ERROR, NOT A RED TEST. Add a member to the policy vocabulary WITHOUT updating the switches. `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck` must FAIL at the `never` assignment. If it passes, the union is not exhaustive by construction and DoD 1 is unmet no matter how green the suite is. Record the typecheck error text.

D2 — THE HUMAN-AUTHORITY CHECK (DoD 5, mandatory). Remove the gate check from the decision function. The NAMED sweep test must go red ON THE REFUSAL ASSERTION for every policy member. Record the test name.

D3 — THE PRINCIPAL REQUIREMENT (DoD 5, mandatory, and independent of D2). Weaken the named-human-principal requirement — accept an empty or non-human principal. A NAMED test must redden on its code-and-layer assertion. If D2 and D3 redden the same single test, they are not pinning two separate facts and one of the two guards is unproven.

D4 — SWEEP CARDINALITY. Remove one member from the generated cases. The count assertion must redden, proving the sweep cannot silently cover fewer members than the vocabulary has.

D5 — ORDERING. Make the decision function consult the policy BEFORE the gate. At least one gated case must redden — this is the drill that proves the gate genuinely short-circuits rather than merely being present.

For each drill record the test name and the assertion that reddened, and confirm it reddened there rather than on a crash.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
TWO MECHANISMS ARE BOTH REQUIRED, and conflating them is the design error this task can most easily ship.

(a) A FROZEN ARRAY gives runtime enumeration — which is what DoD 2's sweep needs, since a test cannot iterate a type.
(b) A DISCRIMINATED UNION plus a `never` exhaustiveness check gives the compile error DoD 1 demands ("adding a member is a compile error at every exhaustive switch over it").
An array alone gives no compile error; a union alone gives nothing to sweep. Ship both, derived from one another so they cannot drift: the union as `(typeof APPROVAL_POLICIES)[number]`, and an `assertNever` in every switch.

THE GATE IS NOT A POLICY MEMBER, and this is the whole task. The tempting shape is a policy value like REQUIRE_HUMAN and calling that the gate. Task rail 1 forbids it: "If your design lets any ApprovalPolicy member approve gated work, the design is wrong." A gate expressed as a policy member is satisfiable by changing the policy — which is exactly what the motivating incident did at scale. The gate must be a SEPARATE per-unit-of-work value consulted FIRST that short-circuits regardless of policy, so the two are not even comparable.

WHY IT MUST BIND TO THE WORK, not the status. In the incident every BLOCKED task was promoted inside a two-minute window and each task's recorded blockedReason was CLEARED by that transition. A gate stored like a status field would have been cleared the same way. It must live in the unit of work's durable identity, and the module comment should say so, because the next reader will otherwise model it as another lifecycle field.

ONE MODULE OR TWO. Planned as ONE module (approval-policy.ts) holding the vocabulary, the gate and the decision function, estimated ~210 lines. That keeps the plan at 6 distinct files with headroom. If it exceeds 250, split the gate into `approval-authority.ts` with its own bridge — named here so the worker is not improvising a split under the cap.

REJECTED: touching the existing `illegal(state, command.kind)` refusal path. DoD 4 requires approvePlan and its reducer arm to keep current behaviour for ungated work with existing tests green and UNMODIFIED. The policy composes in front of them; it does not replace their refusal channel, and the provisional reason channel in approval-gating.ts is explicitly out of scope.

planningNotes.risks:
THE GATE CAN BE SHIPPED SATISFIABLE WITHOUT ANYONE NOTICING. If the gate is modelled as an ApprovalPolicy member, or as a boolean the decision function reads AFTER consulting the policy, then some policy value approves gated work and the suite can still be green — because the happy-path tests never try that combination. DoD 2's requirement is the instrument: enumerate EVERY policy member against a gated unit and assert refusal for each, with the case count pinned equal to the vocabulary size. A sweep that silently produces fewer cases than the vocabulary has members passes while leaving the hole open.

DERIVING THE SWEEP'S EXPECTATION FROM THE ARRAY UNDER TEST makes it compare the array with itself — it then survives both a rename and a deletion. Pin the member NAMES literally and derive only the COUNT from the imported array.

AN EXHAUSTIVE SWITCH IS NOT EXHAUSTIVE WITHOUT THE `never` CHECK. A switch over a union with no default compiles happily when a member is added if every branch returns — TypeScript only errors at the assignment to `never`. Add `assertNever` and prove it: the D1 drill adds a member and requires a COMPILE error, which is a typecheck failure rather than a red test.

THE DELAY MUST BE AN EXPLICIT TYPED VALUE (DoD 1). A proceed-without-human policy whose delay defaults implicitly reproduces the incident's real mechanism — the orchestrating board's 2s auto-approval was a setting nobody stated per unit of work. Make the delay a required field on that arm, so a policy cannot be constructed without stating it.

THE 75-EXPORT PIN WILL REDDEN, and that is correct rather than a problem. packages/core/src/index-surface.test.ts:108 must be updated deliberately, together with the hand-written EXPECTED_EXPORTS catalogue and each new export's declared runtime KIND. Do not "fix" it by leaving the vocabulary unpublished — DoD 1 requires the root publish.

DO NOT MODIFY THE EXISTING APPROVAL TESTS (DoD 4). approvePlan's behaviour for ungated work must be byte-identical and its tests must pass AS WRITTEN. If a change to approvePlan reddens one, the composition is wrong — fix the composition, not the test.

A REFUSAL MUST NOT BE ANSWERED BY THE WRONG LAYER. `illegal(state, command.kind)` already refuses malformed approvals, so a gated-work test that feeds a malformed witness will be refused by the EXISTING guard and prove nothing about the gate. Gated-work cases must be otherwise VALID approvals — correct witness, matching sealed hashes — so the only thing that can refuse them is the new gate. Assert which layer answered.

PURE CONTRACT ONLY (task rail 5): no daemon, no control room, no orchestrator settings file, no migration of existing call sites, and do not touch the provisional reason channel in apps/control-room/src/approvals/approval-gating.ts. Name the consumer tasks instead — Clause 1 requires it, and DoD 6 makes recording them a completion condition.
